summary: This note is a short wiki-style entry on Jakhau, a village and port on the Kutch coast, and on the legendary Jakh Botera who are said to have come ashore there after a shipwreck. It describes the Jakh Botera as tall, fair-complexioned people with an advanced culture, traditionally numbering 72 including at least one woman. It notes an obscure origin theory linking them to Zoroastrian, Iranian or Parsi roots, and says they were credited with ending a cruel king, which earned them godlike status in the region.
one_line: Jakhau is a village and port on the Kutch coast named after the legendary Jakh Botera, shipwrecked people later revered as godlike figures.
key_facts: The village and port of Jakhau are named after the legendary Jakh Botera.
The Jakh Botera were shipwrecked on the Kutch coast and came ashore at Jakhau.
The Jakh Botera are variously described as tall and fair-complexioned with an advanced culture.
Locals name the Jakh Botera Yakshas, meaning demigods.
The traditional number of the Jakh Botera is 72, including at least one woman.
The origins of the Jakh Botera are obscure.
One school of thought holds that the Jakh Botera were of Zoroastrian, Iranian or Parsi origins.
The Jakh Botera are said to have been good at horsemanship, medicine and archery.
A cruel king named Puanra is said to have been controlled or put to an end by the Jakh Botera.
As a result of defeating Puanra, the Jakh Botera attained godlike status in the region.
